prompt: Why does the lesson compare going straight from symptom to action with treating a cough?

choices.text: One symptom, many causes
choices.why: Right: a missed estimate can come from six different places.

choices.text: Because most performance problems are caused by illness
choices.why: Illness is one of six causes, not most of them.

choices.text: Because the manager should send the person to a doctor before any conversation about the work
choices.why: The comparison is about diagnosis before action, not medical referral.

choices.text: Because symptoms disappear on their own
choices.why: Nothing suggests waiting it out.

prompt: Of the six possible causes of a missed estimate, why does the lesson say managers jump to effort and ability first?
hint: Whose problem do they make it?

choices.text: They are the two that make the problem the person’s
choices.why: Right: the other four involve the manager, the work or circumstances.

choices.text: They are the most common causes, according to the research
choices.why: The lesson cites no frequency; it explains the jump by whose problem it becomes.

choices.text: They are the easiest to fix, so a manager naturally starts with them
choices.why: They are often the hardest to fix, and the least likely to be right.

choices.text: HR requires them to be considered first
choices.why: No such requirement.

prompt: Put the three parts of what comes after naming the pattern in order.
items: Only then decide what to do

prompt: What is Mager and Pipe’s most famous question?

choices.text: Do they want to do it?
choices.why: Motivation comes last in the sequence.

choices.text: Have they been trained for it, formally, by somebody qualified to teach it?
choices.why: Training is a response to a skill gap, not the diagnostic question.

choices.text: Who else could do it?
choices.why: Not the question.

choices.text: Could they do it if their life depended on it?
choices.why: Right: if yes, it is not skill; if no, encouragement will not help.

prompt: Why are expectations and environment the first two questions in the sequence?

choices.text: They are the quickest to check
choices.why: Speed is not the reason for the order.

choices.text: Mager and Pipe put them in that order in their original flowchart, and the lesson copies it exactly
choices.why: The lesson adapts their idea, and explains its own ordering.

choices.text: The manager’s own part
choices.why: Right: putting them first stops the manager skipping straight to the person.

choices.text: They are the most common causes
choices.why: The reason given is whose responsibility they are.

prompt: An engineer who finishes quickly always gets handed more work, and has started finishing slowly. Which question in the sequence does that fit?

choices.text: Skill
choices.why: He could do it quickly; he has shown it.

choices.text: Motivation, since he is choosing to work more slowly than he is able to
choices.why: The lesson would ask why first, and the answer is a consequence, not a lack of will.

choices.text: Something makes doing it well unrewarding
choices.why: Right: the consequence of finishing quickly was more work, so he learnt to finish slowly.

choices.text: Something outside work
choices.why: Nothing suggests that.

prompt: Match each finding with the question of the sequence it answers.

pairs.left: nobody told him the team wants to hear about being stuck
the library was undocumented and its author had left
pairs.right: do they have what they need?

pairs.left: he had written good code in the area before
pairs.right: could they do it if their life depended on it?
is something outside work in the way?

prompt: Why does motivation come last in the sequence, by the lesson?

choices.text: It is impossible to measure
choices.why: Measurability is not the reason given.

choices.text: It is the first conclusion managers reach, it is wrong more than it is right, and it hides an earlier cause
choices.why: Right: even when it seems to be will, “why?” leads back to one of the first five.

choices.text: Because managers are not allowed to discuss motivation with the people who report to them
choices.why: Nothing forbids it; it is a matter of order.

choices.text: It never matters
choices.why: The lesson says explicitly that it can matter.

prompt: How did Renata open the diagnostic conversation with Marcos?

choices.text: With what she had got wrong herself
choices.why: Right: starting with the manager’s part changes what the person is willing to say.

choices.text: By repeating the three examples from the first conversation
choices.why: That conversation had already named the pattern; this one was for learning why.

choices.text: By asking whether he still cared about the work, since that was the question on everybody’s mind
choices.why: She deliberately did not ask that.

choices.text: With the improvement plan
choices.why: There was no plan yet.

prompt: What did Marcos believe a good engineer does, that explained part of the pattern?

choices.text: Writes no tests, to move faster
choices.why: Nothing like that came up.

choices.text: Never revises an estimate once it has been given to the team and to the product manager
choices.why: He was embarrassed to revise, but that came from the same belief about asking for help.

choices.text: Solves problems alone
choices.why: Right: asking for help felt like admitting he was not good enough.

choices.text: Works long hours
choices.why: Not what he said.

prompt: Which responses followed the diagnostic conversation? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Documenting the notification library with Yara
choices.why: Yes: for the environment cause.

choices.text: Moving him down a level
choices.why: No: skill on the code was not the problem.

choices.text: An immediate improvement plan
choices.why: No: that came a month later, only where things had not changed.

choices.text: Written expectations about raising problems and revising estimates
choices.why: Yes: for the expectations cause.

choices.text: Two on-call weeks off the rota, arranged with Sônia
choices.why: Yes: for the cause outside work.

prompt: Renata told Marcos he did not need to say what the problem outside work was; she only wanted to know whether it was a ___.
A manager says: “She’s been missing deadlines for a month. She clearly doesn’t care any more.” Using this lesson, what is the strongest objection?
hint: Where does that conclusion sit in the sequence?

choices.text: He has jumped to the last question without checking the five before it
choices.why: Right: motivation is the conclusion reached first and often wrongly.

choices.text: A month is too short to notice anything
choices.why: A month is long enough to notice; the problem is the conclusion.

choices.text: He should start an improvement plan straight away rather than keep waiting for things to change
choices.why: A plan before a diagnosis is acting on a guess.

choices.text: He should ask her colleagues
choices.why: Not the lesson’s method; the first step is the sequence and then her.
